Tuning context length with rolling-origin resampling

Source: vignettes/rolling-origin-tuning.Rmd
rolling-origin-tuning.Rmd

How much history should a foundation model condition on? More context is not always better — it can dilute recent signal and cost compute. Because tsfm exposes context_length as a tunable dials parameter, you can answer this empirically with the standard tidymodels tuning machinery over rolling-origin (time-aware) resamples, rather than random cross-validation that would leak the future into the past.

The code below uses the executable stub fixture to demonstrate the mechanics. It is not a foundation-model benchmark; repeat the workflow with TimesFM only after that checkpoint passes the package’s support gates.

The spec

Mark context_length for tuning; everything else is fixed through the engine:

library(tsfm)
library(parsnip)
library(workflows)
library(tune)
library(dials)
library(rsample)

spec <- tsfm_reg(context_length = tune()) |>
  set_engine("tsfm",
             model_id = "stub",
             index    = "date",
             id       = "store")

wf <- workflow() |>
  add_formula(demand ~ date) |>
  add_model(spec)

Rolling-origin resamples

rsample::sliding_period() builds analysis/assessment splits that always move forward in time — the assessment window is strictly after its analysis window:

folds <- sliding_period(
  train_df,
  index  = date,
  period = "month",
  lookback   = Inf,   # expanding-origin: use all history up to each split
  assess_stop = 1     # score one month ahead
)

Search

Give context_length a range and let tune_grid() score each candidate with a proper (quantile-aware) metric:

grid <- grid_regular(
  context_length(range = c(64L, 512L)),
  levels = 5
)

res <- tune_grid(
  wf,
  resamples = folds,
  grid      = grid,
  metrics   = metric_set(yardstick::rmse, yardstick::mae)
)

show_best(res, metric = "rmse")
best <- select_best(res, metric = "rmse")

final_fit <- finalize_workflow(wf, best) |>
  fit(data = train_df)

Notes

  • context_length bounds the most recent history retained by each fitted engine; the end-to-end behavior is covered with the stub in package tests.
  • The heavy per-candidate cost is inference, not training (these are zero-shot models), so keep the grid small and prefer sliding_period() windows that reflect your real forecast horizon.
